intelligence.human_view: Two things in one message, and they are opposites in the best way: keep, and fix. Keep: the end view is beautiful — the red orb with the gold N, elevated, official — one of the most beautiful elegant pieces the team did, and it stays exactly as it is, never redesigned. Fix: it vanishes on refresh, so a citizen who reaches the end and reloads loses the very thing that makes the agreement feel official. An end that disappears is not an end — it is a moment you cannot return to. The fix is persistence, not redesign: the end state survives a refresh and is reachable directly, without walking the deck again. The checker proves it the way a citizen would: reach the end, refresh, and the end is still there — orb, portrait, text, legal link, I agree — at 390 and at 1851×1009. What is good is kept verbatim; what is broken is the state, not the look.
intelligence.simple_view: Imagine you build the most beautiful tower out of blocks — red and gold and so tall and pretty! And then someone bumps the table and — poof! — it's gone! That would be so sad, right? So we make sure your beautiful tower STAYS there, even if you leave and come back! The red N orb is the prettiest tower — it stays!
intelligence.grandma_view: It's like this, love — imagine the most beautiful picture, dear, red and gold and so elegant — and every time you blink, it's gone! Oh no, love — a beautiful thing like that should stay right where you left it, so when you come back, there it is, just as lovely. That's what we do, dear — we keep the beautiful end right there, even after a refresh.
